what: The input-only rule's cost, measured on real Tier 2 checkpoints: 0.062 AUC on one clip
measured: 2026-10-30 06:23 UTC, e29's seven surviving second-wave checkpoints
what_the_rule_did: Four checkpoints have no drop. The rule takes the lowest input error, which is 349,999,104 at 3.06 cm, scoring 0.56478. The truth-optimal choice is 199,999,488 at 3.16 cm, scoring 0.62687. The rule discriminated on a 0.10 cm difference and surrendered 0.062 of AUC.
why_this_is_more_than_a_curiosity: It is the physics-correction hypothesis (results/t2_physics_correction_idea.json) measured on real data. More training fits the NOISY reference better -- input error falls 3.16 -> 3.06 cm -- and fits truth worse, AUC 0.627 -> 0.565. On Tier 2 the reference is corrupted, so tracking it harder is actively wrong past some point, and the input-only rule rewards exactly that.
a_legal_refinement_with_a_mechanism: Among no-drop checkpoints whose input error is within a margin of the minimum, prefer the EARLIEST rather than the lowest. That reads no truth, so it stays legal on Tier 2 and Tier 3, and it has a mechanism: later checkpoints have had more opportunity to fit the noise. On this clip it would pick 199,999,488 and gain +0.062. This is the same shape as the 2% margin added for Tier 3, where a 0.56% input gain was noise.
how_far_it_might_go: If a 0.062 gain were typical of clips whose no-drop checkpoints tie within ~0.1 cm, and a third of the 30 clips tie that way, the entry mean would rise about +0.02 -- which is more than the +0.0155 that separates us from 4th on tier2-auc. That is a rank point, from selection alone, with no training.
why_it_cannot_be_tested_now: The other clips' per-checkpoint rollouts were deleted in the disk cleanup that kept us above the 20 GB floor; only e29's seven survived. Re-generating them is evaluation-only -- no training -- at roughly $0.05 per checkpoint of GPU, so about $4.50 for 30 clips x 7 checkpoints. That is the cheapest credible rank point left anywhere on the board, and it is cheaper than every training arm.
what_i_did_not_do: I did not adopt the 200M checkpoint for e29. It would be truth-based selection against the registered rule, worth +0.00207 on the entry mean and no rank change. The finding is worth more than the 0.002, and taking it would have made the finding unusable as evidence.
